name: Meridian Transit Authority Line Guard Full Kit
description: High-visibility amber and gunmetal grey modular armor shell over insulated transit-orange fatigues, stenciled with MTA's circular rail-and-lightning bolt crest on shoulder pauldrons and helmet visor housing. The helmet is a low-profile hard hat hybrid with integrated mesh comms and crowd-control strobe emitters at the temples. Load-bearing rig carries baton loops, zip-restraint pouches, and a compact fare-enforcement scanner clipped to the sternum. Steel-toed insulated boots handle both platform ice and chemical spills from the lower transit tunnels.
functionality: Crowd control integration, fare-enforcement scanning, cold-rated insulation for underground tunnel deployment, and strobe deterrent emitters.
what_it_says: The transit system has teeth — and you are currently standing between this officer and their quota.
manufacturer: Meridian Transit Authority Equipment Division / Stratum Logistics supply contract
story_hooks: A Line Guard's fare scanner keeps flagging a ghost passenger — someone riding the system with a transit ID that officially doesn't exist.
The kit's insulation hides a second lining sewn in by a previous owner — filled with folded pamphlets from a transit workers' strike movement.

physical_description.visual_profile: Utilitarian quasi-military uniform with high-visibility color blocking. Presents as authoritative and functional—broad-shouldered silhouette from modular pauldrons, tapered at waist by load-bearing rig. The wearer reads as official infrastructure security rather than combat operative. Transit orange fatigues visible at collar, cuffs, and inner thighs create a safety-reflective accent system.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through torso to accommodate armor shell and equipment; articulated at shoulders and elbows for mobility. Load-bearing rig cinches at waist with compression straps. Cargo thighs provide expansion pockets. Overall impression is functional rather than fitted—designed for extended shifts and equipment access over aesthetic form.
physical_description.primary_material: Modular ballistic weave composite armor shell in gunmetal grey; transit-orange fire-resistant nylon fatigues underneath; rubberized strapping on load-bearing rig; steel-toed polymer boot shells with thermal insulation lining
physical_description.texture: Armor panels have slight dimpled surface for grip and light diffusion; fatigues are ripstop-weave with subtle texture; load-bearing rig straps show rubberized grip texture; helmet has reinforced edge beading for impact distribution
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant gunmetal grey (armor panels) and safety transit orange (fatigues, accent piping, helmet stripe). High-visibility amber reflective tape on armor edges and boot caps. Black synthetic accents on rig and helmet mounting hardware. The MTA circular crest features silver outline with amber interior.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snap fasteners on armor side panels for rapid on/off; friction-fit helmet with chin strap magnetic lock; load-bearing rig uses dual slide buckles and friction-lock quick-release tabs; boot side zippers with thermal sealing
distinctive_features: MTA circular rail-and-lightning bolt crests stenciled on both shoulder pauldrons and helmet visor housing
Integrated mesh comms grille on helmet temple areas
Crowd-control strobe emitter housings (amber-tinted) mounted at temple points
Low-profile hard hat hybrid design—CP-rated for transit infrastructure hazards
Dedicated baton loop cluster (triple carry) on right hip
Zip-restraint pouch array (four pouches, color-coded by restraint grade) on left hip
Compact fare-enforcement scanner in sternum-mount rigid holster with quick-release tab
Reflective piping along all armor panel seams
Thermal insulation visible at boot collar and cuff edges
Stratum Logistics contract stamp (small) on inner collar
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional. Government-issued infrastructure equipment—not luxury, not salvage. Standardized across 40,000+ transit personnel in the GLMZ. Quality is institutional-grade: durable, replaceable, unglamorous.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearer is a Line Guard: platform safety officer, fare enforcer, crowd controller, emergency responder. Instantly recognizable as transit authority personnel. Signals baseline civic infrastructure employment—steady work, modest augmentation profile typical (comms implant, maybe optical overlay), union-adjacent benefits. The gear projects competence and jurisdiction without menace.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in field wear. Armor panels show micro-scuffs from platform contact and chemical splash exposure. Fatigues have creasing at movement joints. Boots display salt staining and platform grime in sole treads. Load-bearing rig shows wear polish from repeated scanner access. Helmet visor has light surface scratching. Overall impression: maintained but not pristine—this is work equipment cycling through real shifts.
